collins.hedgehog: None. Collins's comparison company had no Hedgehog Concept. It drifted into unrelated diversification and failed to choose and defend a field it could be best at against P&G.
hedgehog_key_points: should narrow to a core it can be best at (consumer tissue/towels) or admit it cannot beat P&G
collins.stop_doing: Stop unrelated diversification (furniture, audio-visual aids, coatings) and stop treating past dominance as a strategy. Confront P&G's entry.
stop_doing_key_points: stop relying on past dominance and list-price cuts
collins.leader_type: Not Level 5. A leadership vacuum followed by a series of chairmen; later the outsider 'Chainsaw' Al Dunlap (1994), whom Collins cites as the opposite of Level 5.
brutal_facts: falling return on equity and earnings
P&G's national entry into premium tissue with superior softness
acquisitions worth about $200M that are not profitable

later_history: Lost ground to P&G (Charmin) and other rivals through the 1970s-80s. A disastrous capacity expansion in 1990. Record loss of $277M in 1993. Dunlap cut about one third of the workforce and sold more than $2B in assets in 1994. Absorbed by Kimberly-Clark in 1995 and ceased to exist as an independent company.
notes: Direct comparison company for A01. Collins's appendix gives K-C's transition as 1972 (window 1972-87); the dossier is dated 1971, just before it.
